title: Death, Hearts & Healing
h1: Minecraft Hearts Explained: Death Penalties, Healing and Crystal Hearts
description: Why Minecraft health doesn't regenerate on this survival rework, what dying costs in maximum hearts, and how to heal with food, potions and Crystal Hearts.
intro: Health works differently on this survival rework: natural regeneration is off, hunger is gone, and death costs maximum hearts rather than items. These answers explain the rules in plain language. MatchaSMP is the worked example.

items.q: Why doesn't my health regenerate in Minecraft?
items.a: On this survival rework, natural health regeneration is turned off. You heal with food effects, potions and special items instead, so bring food when you explore.

items.q: Does hunger matter in a Minecraft survival rework?
items.a: Hunger is effectively gone on MatchaSMP: you won't starve, and food is valued for its effects instead of filling a hunger bar.

items.q: Which items heal you in a Minecraft survival rework?
items.a: On MatchaSMP you heal with foods that have healing effects, potions and special items. Food is valued for its effects rather than for filling a bar.

items.q: How do I get hearts back in Minecraft after dying?
items.a: Crystal Hearts add a maximum heart back, up to a total of 30. Each death costs one maximum heart, so Crystal Hearts are how you recover lost ground.

items.q: What happens to my items when I die in Minecraft survival?
items.a: On MatchaSMP you keep your inventory and XP when you die. Each death removes 1 maximum heart instead, and thrown ender pearls don't vanish.

items.q: What is the minimum number of hearts in Minecraft on a server?
items.a: On MatchaSMP, which runs on Easy, you never drop below 10 hearts from deaths.

items.q: What is a maximum heart in Minecraft?
items.a: A maximum heart is the most hearts you can reach. On MatchaSMP each death removes one, and Crystal Hearts add one back, up to a total of 30.

items.q: Do you lose XP when you die in Minecraft?
items.a: No. On MatchaSMP you keep your XP on death, along with your inventory.
